objective: Three modules of the `stockroom` package have nothing to do with inventory or orders: `money.py`, `textutil.py` and `dates.py`. Move them into a new subpackage `stockroom/util/` (as `stockroom/util/money.py`, `stockroom/util/textutil.py` and `stockroom/util/dates.py`) and let the rest of the package import them from there. The old module paths `stockroom.money`, `stockroom.textutil` and `stockroom.dates` must keep working for outside callers, but only as thin re-export shims. The project is installed from `pyproject.toml`, so the new subpackage has to be part of what gets packaged. This is a pure refactor: the moved functions behave exactly as before, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `stockroom.util` is a package, and the functions of the three moved modules report `stockroom.util.money`, `stockroom.util.textutil` and `stockroom.util.dates` as their `__module__`

`stockroom.money`, `stockroom.textutil` and `stockroom.dates` still import, and every public function they offered (`format_money`, `parse_money`, `split_evenly`; `align`, `plural`, `slugify`, `truncate`; `add_months`, `days_between`, `days_in_month`, `format_date`, `month_key`, `months_between`, `parse_date`) is the very same object as in the new module; each shim lists exactly these names in `__all__`
Each shim contains only its docstring, imports and `__all__`, no definitions of its own

No module of the package other than the three shims imports `stockroom.money`, `stockroom.textutil` or `stockroom.dates` by the old path (neither relative nor absolute); they import the `util` modules instead
The `packages` list of `[tool.setuptools]` in `pyproject.toml` names both `stockroom` and `stockroom.util`

The moved money functions give the same results and raise the same errors as before (`parse_money` with and without `$` and thousands commas, refusing text that is not an amount; `format_money`; `split_evenly` including its `ValueError` for zero parts)

The moved text functions give the same results and raise the same errors as before (`slugify`, `truncate` of short text and its `ValueError` for width 0, `align` for `left`, `right`, `center` and an unknown name, `plural`)

The moved date functions give the same results and raise the same errors as before (`parse_date` and its `ParseError`, `format_date`, `month_key`, `days_in_month` outside February, February of a year that is not a leap year and a month out of range, `add_months` forwards and backwards across year ends with clamping to the last day, `days_between`, `months_between`)

The modules that use the helpers (`csvio`, `jsonio`, `orders`, `report`, `cli`) still work together: orders read from CSV and written back are identical, and the revenue per month and the sales summary of those orders are the same as before
